blocks.text: The **Indus/Harappan Civilisation** spread across a vast area of the north-west subcontinent, with major cities strung along the **Indus and (dried) Saraswati-Ghaggar-Hakra** systems. Each key site — **Harappa, Mohenjodaro, Dholavira, Lothal, Kalibangan, Rakhigarhi** — is associated with distinctive finds that are frequent exam facts.

rows: **Ravi** (Punjab, Pakistan); first excavated (1921, Daya Ram Sahni); granaries, cemetery R-37, workmen's quarters.
**Indus** (Sindh, Pakistan); **Great Bath, Great Granary, Dancing Girl, Priest-King, Pashupati seal**.
**Rann of Kutch (Gujarat)**; unique **water-harvesting/reservoirs**, signboard, three-part city; **UNESCO site**.
**Gujarat (Bhogava)**; **dockyard** (maritime trade), bead factory, rice husk, fire-altars.
**Haryana** — the **largest IVC site** in India (Ghaggar plain).

items: Match site to signature find: Mohenjodaro-Great Bath/Dancing Girl, Lothal-dockyard, Kalibangan-ploughed field, Dholavira-water reservoirs, Rakhigarhi-largest in India.
Harappa was the first site excavated (1921); rivers: Harappa-Ravi, Mohenjodaro-Indus.

prelimsPointers: **Harappa (Ravi, Pakistan)** — first excavated in **1921** (Daya Ram Sahni); granaries, cemetery R-37.
**Mohenjodaro (Indus, Sindh)** — **Great Bath, Great Granary, Dancing Girl, Priest-King, Pashupati seal**.
**Dholavira (Kutch, Gujarat)** — advanced **water-harvesting & reservoirs**; 'signboard'; a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**.
Other sites — **Chanhudaro (beads, no citadel), Banawali, Surkotada (horse bones debated), Ropar**.
mainsAngles: Discuss the major sites of the Indus Valley Civilisation and their significance.

glossary.definition: 'Mound of the dead' — the largest Harappan city, site of the Great Bath and Dancing Girl.
A Harappan port town in Gujarat with a dockyard, evidencing maritime trade.
The largest Indus Valley site located in India (Haryana).
